subject: QuantifyAI: evaluation playbook and baseline comparison
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Parker <ellen.parker@quantifyai.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@quantifyai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 15:21:00 -0700
Subject: QuantifyAI: evaluation playbook and baseline comparison

Hi Ellen / Samir —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call today. Quick recap and a proposed evaluation playbook so we can get a 2-week trial running next week: 

Summary of needs (from call)
- Primary task: customer support triage + short-form answer generation for policy-related queries.
- Success criteria: match or exceed current internal baseline on intent accuracy and reduce hallucination incidents in policy responses.
- Nonfunctional constraints: data residency in US, P95 latency target ~120ms, cost sensitivity for high-volume endpoints.

Proposed next steps (high level)
1) Trial scope: 2-week A/B-style trial comparing your baseline (qai-prod-1.3) against 3 curated open variants.
2) Evaluation matrix & metrics: intent accuracy, helpfulness score (annotator-rated), hallucination rate (binary checklist), latency (P50/P95), token cost.
3) Prompt sets & blind eval: we’ll run your internal prompt set plus a Redwood-adapted prompt bundle. Annotators will be blind to the model.
4) Logistics: we’ll need a signed scope doc + sample prompt set to kick off. I attached an initial prompt bundle and a template for capture.

Recommended open models to include in the trial (initial suggestions)
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (instruction-tuned)
- Llama-2-13B-chat (13B chat-tuned, quantized run for latency)
- Falcon-7B-Instruct (fast small-footprint option)

Acceptance thresholds (proposal)
- Intent accuracy: >= 95% of baseline (ideally meet or exceed)
- Hallucination incidents: <= 2% on policy-sensitive prompts (measured with a fixed hallucination checklist)
- Latency P95: <= 120ms when deployed on comparable dedicated capacity
- Annotator helpfulness: mean score within 0.1 of baseline on 5-point scale

Attachments: prompt_sets_quantifyai_v1.json, eval_template_qai.xlsx, trial_scope_summary.pdf

Can you confirm: 1) we have permission to include qai-prod-1.3 in the A/B? 2) target start date of Mon Aug 9 works?

If yes, we’ll provision a trial endpoint, seed the prompt sets, and schedule a short kickoff (30m) to align annotator instructions.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this fast.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Ellen Parker <ellen.parker@quantifyai.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Khan <samir.khan@quantifyai.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuantifyAI: evaluation playbook and baseline comparison

Diego —

Thanks for the clear recap and the fast turnaround. High-level yes — we want to see if open alternatives can reach feature parity while lowering cost. A few clarifications before we sign the scope: 

Questions / concerns
- Baseline to include: yes, you have permission to include qai-prod-1.3. We’ll also ask engineering for a read-only artifact (inference logs sample) to help match input distributions.
- Hallucination definition: can you share the exact checklist you’ll use? For us, hallucinations on policy content are high severity and need explicit examples.
- Privacy & data handling: all trial requests must be logged and retained in our tenant; we need assurance that test data will not leave our contracted region.
- Prompt set: the attached prompt_sets_quantifyai_v1.json looks good but can you add 150 domain-specific cases for product policy escalation? We’ll upload a sample pack by EOD Wednesday.

Timing
- Aug 9 start is OK if we have the scope doc signed by Aug 6. We’d like results within two weeks and a short decision sync the week after.

Thanks — Samir and I will coordinate the artifact delivery.

Best,
Ellen Parker
Head of Product
QuantifyAI

Subject: Re: QuantifyAI: evaluation playbook and baseline comparison

Ellen —

Appreciate the quick notes. Below are concrete answers and the evaluation design we'll run if you approve.

1) Hallucination checklist (short version)- Binary label per response: hallucination_yes / hallucination_no.- If yes: reason tags (unsupported_fact, contradicted_by_policy, invented_contact_details).

2) Data residency / logging- Trial endpoints will be provisioned in a US-only VPC for your tenant. Logs for the trial will stay in your tenant project and can be exported to your S3. We will not use trial data to train models.

3) Prompt set augmentation- Please upload the 150 domain-specific cases by EOD Wed; we'll integrate and produce a final balanced bundle (prompt_sets_quantifyai_v1.1.json).

Evaluation design (proposal)
- Models deployed: qai-prod-1.3 (your baseline), Mistral-Instruct-7B, Llama-2-13B-chat, Falcon-7B-Instruct.- Runs: each model evaluated on the full prompt bundle (n~2,500 examples including the 150 added cases).- Annotator eval: blind Rater set (6 annotators, majority label) for hallucination and helpfulness.
- Metrics & thresholds: intent accuracy (>=95% of baseline), hallucination rate (<=2% absolute, and <= baseline), mean helpfulness delta (>= -0.1), latency P95 (<= 120ms on equivalent dedicated capacity).

Blind evaluation & tie-breaking- If an open model matches intent accuracy and hallucination thresholds within statistical margin, we recommend a secondary qualitative review (10% of samples) run by your SMEs.

Operational notes
- Cost estimate: we'll share a conservative cost projection for the trial once models & batch sizes are finalized.
- Deliverables: live trial endpoints, raw run outputs, blinded annotation spreadsheet, summary recommendations doc.

Next steps to start on Aug 9
1) Confirm scope & sign trial_scope_summary.pdf by COB Aug 6.
2) Upload 150 domain cases to the Drive folder.
3) Kickoff 30m sync on Aug 9 (we’ll share a calendar invite).

If that all looks good I’ll get infrastructure queued and Neha will own the annotation plan on our side.

Thanks,
Diego
